metadata.title: [Kernel][SM70] Keep 32x32 UE8M0 block-FP8 dense weights in FP8 on Volta
metadata.body:
> Contributed by PLI Labs (Proprietary Legal Intelligence). The same branch is also published at [ProprietaryLegal/1Cat-vLLM](https://github.com/ProprietaryLegal/1Cat-vLLM/tree/feat/sm70-fp8-block32-weight-only), and the patch series, tests and measurements are on Hugging Face at [ProprietaryLegal/sm70-fp8-block32-kernels](https://huggingface.co/ProprietaryLegal/sm70-fp8-block32-kernels).

## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ships its dense projections as E4M3 with one UE8M0 (power-of-two) scale per 32 × 32 block (`weight_block_size: [32, 32]`, `scale_fmt: ue8m0`). The SM70 FP8 linear path admitted only `[128, 128]` to TurboMind. A `[32, 32]` layer fell through to the generic selector, which picks Marlin. SM70 Marlin FP8 supports only group -1/128, and the layer failed in `process_weights_after_loading`. The only working route was `VLLM_SM70_FP8_TURBOMIND=0`, which dequantizes every weight to FP16 at load time and doubles dense weight memory.

This PR keeps such weights in FP8 on Volta:

- **Native ops:** add a `Config_E4M3` `GroupSizeV=32` tile family (M 8..128) to `sm70_884_8.cu`, next to the group-128 list. `fp8_sm70_prepare`, `fp8_gemm_sm70_out` and `fp8_sm70_dequantize_out` accept `group_size=32`. The TurboMind dispatcher keys on group size, so group-128 callers get the same kernels as before. The exact-8K pre-scaled prefill and the fused gated-SiLU variants stay group-128 only and reject group 32 explicitly.
- **`quantization/utils/sm70_fp8_block32.py`:** stores one TurboMind-packed copy per weight (1 B/param plus one FP16 scale per 32 K-values of each row, 1/16 extra). Three kernels read that copy, selected by batch size inside the opaque custom op `torch.ops.vllm.sm70_fp8_block32_linear`, so Dynamo does not guard on M:
  - a Triton GEMV that reads the TurboMind panel layout directly (`[N/32][K/8][32][8]`, byte order 0,2,1,3 within each 8-byte chunk). It decodes E4M3 with integer ops and accumulates in FP32, and it can write FP16 or FP32 output.
  - TurboMind group-32 HMMA.
  - a transient FP16 rebuild of the weight followed by cuBLAS.
- **`fp8.py`:** under the default policy, a `[32, 32]` layer becomes a candidate. After loading:
  - If every scale is an exact power of two in [2^-14, 2^7], the weight is packed for these kernels.
  - Otherwise it is dequantized to FP16 at load time (the existing `dequant_fallback` route) with a warning that names the reason.
  - `[128, 128]` layers, grouped `is_bmm` layers, `kernel_config.sm70_fp8.enabled=False` (`VLLM_SM70_FP8_TURBOMIND=0`) and the forced Marlin backend keep their previous routes.

### Exactness and range guard

An E4M3 value is a multiple of 2^-9 with at most 4 significant bits, and |v| ≤ 448 = 1.75 × 2^8. Therefore v × 2^e is an exact FP16 value (subnormals included) for e ∈ [-15, 7], and e = 8 would turn 448 into 114688 > 65504. With the scale itself an FP16 normal (e ≥ -14), scales in [2^-14, 2^7] make every kernel multiply exactly the weights of the load-time FP16 dequantization. The paths differ from it only in FP32 accumulation order.

`prepare` refuses two cases loudly:
- scales outside that window, or scales that are not powers of two;
- E4M3 NaN codes (0x7F/0xFF), which the bit-level decoders would otherwise turn into finite ±480.

V4.1's dense exponents are -13…-6. A per-layer exception, such as an auxiliary projection with exponents down to -18, is caught by the window check and takes the FP16 load-time route.

### Dispatch (FP16 output; measured, see the table below)

| rows M | kernel |
| --- | --- |
| M ≤ 2 (M ≤ 4 when N ≤ 1152) | Triton GEMV |
| up to 16 (N < 1536), 32 (1536 ≤ N < 4096), 64 (N ≥ 4096, K < 1024), 128 (N ≥ 4096, K ≥ 1024) | TurboMind group-32 |
| above | FP16 rebuild + cuBLAS |

With FP32 output, the GEMV serves M ≤ 8 and the rebuild + cuBLAS path serves larger M. FP32 output is available through the helper API. A generic `LinearBase` layer always uses FP16 output.

## Test Plan

Build `_C` for `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.0`, then run:

```console
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_sm70_fp8_block32.py tests/quantization/test_sm70_fp8_block32_route.py
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_sm70_fp8_block32.py --out results/
python -m tools.sm70_route_snapshot --category fp8-policy --baseline-ref origin/main
```

I also ran the 22 existing SM70 FP8 suites (QPN8 block FP8, prefill exact dense, workspace AOT reload, kernel selection, policy snapshots, PP2×TP4 QPN8, compressed-tensors fast paths, Marlin BMM dequant and others) on this branch and on `origin/main`.

## Test Result

Hardware: V100-SXM2-32GB on one 4-card NVLink board, SM clock capped at 1477 MHz, 180 W power limit. The SM clock drops to about 950–1100 MHz in the heavy phases of the benchmark. Driver 580.159.03, CUDA 12.8.93, torch 2.10.0+cu128. Each figure is a CUDA-graph replay of 20 back-to-back calls, with the weight copies rotated so the 6 MB L2 never serves a repeat. `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction=False`.

- **New tests: 38/38 pass.**
  - One-hot exact decode, bitwise on every kernel, over all 254 finite codes and the window ends: subnormal products at 2^-14, and 57344 at 2^7.
  - Products against the FP64 dequantization at 11 shapes × 16 M values that cover every dispatch boundary. FP16 output stays within the FP16 floor (rel-RMS < 3e-4) and within 1.5× the FP16-weight cuBLAS error. FP32 output stays at accumulation-order level.
  - Refusals: e = 8, e = -15, e = -18, non-power-of-two scales, NaN codes, bad shapes, and the group-32 pre-scaled and gated-SiLU variants.
  - Group-128 ops unchanged.
  - Route checks: power-of-two FP32 and E8M0 scale parameters, inexact scales falling back to FP16 at load, NaN codes failing loudly, `is_bmm`, both policy switches, and `[128, 128]` unchanged.
- **Existing SM70 FP8 suites:** 435 passed and 4 failed on this branch; 435 passed and the same 4 failed on `origin/main` (NVFP4 fingerprint hash, two workspace-capacity cases, and one order-dependent compressed-tensors channel case).
- **Route snapshot:** 324 configurations, 0 changes.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash per layer per GPU at TP4, FP16-output dense projections (wq_a+wkv, wq_b, indexer wq_b, 2 × wo_a). Dense weight bytes for this set fall from 63.5 MiB (FP16) to 33.7 MiB.

| M | FP16 weights + cuBLAS (µs) | FP8 block-32 (µs) | change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 115.2 | 74.2 | −36% |
| 2 | 129.3 | 93.8 | −27% |
| 4 | 132.1 | 103.4 | −22% |
| 8 | 135.4 | 112.4 | −17% |
| 16 | 137.7 | 125.3 | −9% |
| 32 | 185.2 | 209.7 | +13% |
| 64 | 233.7 | 287.1 | +23% |
| 128 | 430.5 | 414.8 | −4% |
| 512 | 687.4 | 782.6 | +14% |
| 4096 | 4994.4 | 4335.4 | −13% |

Per projection at decode sizes (µs, FP8 vs FP16 weights; G = GEMV, T = TurboMind):

| projection (N × K) | M=1 | M=2 | M=4 | M=8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| wq_a+wkv (1792 × 5120) | 19.3 vs 30.1 G | 26.0 vs 34.0 G | 27.1 vs 34.4 T | 29.5 vs 35.3 T |
| wq_b (8192 × 1280) | 19.6 vs 31.5 G | 21.8 vs 36.8 G | 22.0 vs 38.4 T | 22.9 vs 40.2 T |
| indexer wq_b (4096 × 1280) | 13.5 vs 17.9 G | 15.0 vs 20.2 G | 15.4 vs 20.3 T | 15.9 vs 20.5 T |
| wo_a group (1024 × 4096) | 10.9 vs 17.9 G | 15.5 vs 19.1 G | 19.4 vs 19.5 G | 22.1 vs 19.7 T |
| wo_b (5120 × 2048) | 20.3 vs 30.7 G | 23.8 vs 31.8 G | 23.6 vs 32.1 T | 27.8 vs 32.7 T |
| shared w13 (1152 × 5120) | 14.0 vs 24.3 G | 19.5 vs 23.8 G | 22.8 vs 24.3 G | 27.4 vs 24.8 T |
| shared w2 (5120 × 576) | 9.8 vs 12.3 G | 10.0 vs 10.8 G | 10.7 vs 10.9 T | 11.9 vs 11.0 T |

The kernel thresholds pick, at each measured size, the fastest kernel that reads the single FP8 copy. Kernel-level results do not cover a full model. No end-to-end serving result is claimed here.

## Limitations and follow-ups

- **One FP8 copy costs time at some sizes.** From M ≈ 32 upward the FP8 copy costs time against FP16 weights at several shapes: about +13…+23% at M 32–64 and +14% at M 512 for the V4.1 layer set, and up to +75% on the narrow wo_a group at M 32–64. Large M (4096) is at parity or faster. Users who prefer FP16 speed over memory keep `kernel_config.sm70_fp8.enabled=False`. A dedicated per-format switch, or an optional FP16 prefill copy like `block_qpn8_volta_turbomind_prefill`, is a possible follow-up.
- **Small-K shapes:** the shared-expert down projection at TP8 (K = 288) is slower than FP16 cuBLAS from M = 2.
- **TurboMind tuning:** the group-32 tiles lose to cuBLAS FP16 at M 32–64 for narrow N. TurboMind tile selection is non-monotonic at M 128–512 (for example, wq_a+wkv is faster through TurboMind at M 128/256 than through the rebuild). A per-shape tile table or `TM_MAX_M` would recover this.
- **FP32-output TurboMind epilogue:** row-parallel outputs that must stay in FP32 (V4.1 `wo_b`, shared-expert down) have only the GEMV (M ≤ 8) and the rebuild path today.
- **Grouped g32 BMM** for `is_bmm` layers (V4.1 `wo_a`, 2 groups per TP4 rank): these layers keep the existing grouped route.
- **Power limit:** the board ran at 180 W, so compute-bound rows (M ≥ 128) carry clock throttling. Decode rows are bandwidth-bound and less sensitive to the clock.
